public_rationale: The deadline has passed, and ASI-Arch supplies substantial counterevidence: agents proposed and tested neural-architecture changes in 2025. That is more than routine coding assistance. But the available record does not clearly settle Marcus's stronger requirement of fundamentally new ideas. DiscoRL addresses a different discovery mechanism, while METR's narrower analysis cannot establish a field-wide absence. A definitive verdict would depend on a novelty threshold Marcus did not supply.
limitations: Research performance and conceptual novelty are different questions.
The principal direct candidate was initially a developer-authored preprint.
A single realized outcome would not establish the calibration of the speaker's probability judgment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agents are very unlikely to be contributing fundamentally new ideas to AI research by the end of 2025.

statement.excerpt: It would be astounding if AI agents were actually contributing fundamentally new ideas to AI by the end of year.
statement.document_title: The “AI 2027” Scenario: How realistic is it?

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a strong expectation against agents making substantive original contributions to AI research by that deadline.
In context, the agents are LLM-based research agents. Conventional automated search or meta-learning is relevant context but is not automatically the same subject.

A contribution may involve human collaborators. It must include a substantive original research idea with demonstrated value; routine implementation, parameter tuning, or benchmark improvement alone is insufficient.
The phrase is assessed as a directional forecast, not a numerical probability claim.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive assessment of research completed by the deadline establishes that agent contributions remained implementation assistance or incremental optimization without substantive original research ideas.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one documented contribution made by an LLM-based agent by December 31, 2025 establishes a substantive original AI-research idea, its attribution to the agent, and its demonstrated value.

evidence.explanation: ASI-Arch reports agent-generated neural architectures and comparative experiments, making it substantial counterevidence to the forecast. The report does not by itself settle whether these architecture changes meet the stronger threshold of fundamentally new ideas.

DiscoRL demonstrates automated discovery of learning rules with tested performance. It uses meta-learning from agents' experience, so treating it as an LLM research agent contributing an idea would change the scope of Marcus's contextual claim.

evidence.locator: AI agents have recently contributed, but their current contributions appear relatively shallow
evidence.explanation: The analysis cautions against equating agent-attributed training improvements with deep research ideas. Its records extend into March 2026 and cover one task family, so it cannot establish the global 2025 forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A technical assessment of a contribution completed by December 31, 2025 that establishes agent attribution, substantive novelty against prior work, and demonstrated value; or a sufficiently comprehensive review establishing that no contributions crossed that threshold.
